Trust Balance stat button, the Trust tab (alert, matter ledger, 4 buttons, evergreen retainer, transactions table)

flectra.why: The legal vertical installs all four modules together (legal_billing and legal_trust are its MVP phases), so a lawyer sees the three inherited views on every case.

dialogs.note: only its deposit fields, as the Deposit button opens it

flectra.note: the base view alone: 151 field nodes, 14 tabs, 10 tables, 9 smart buttons; legal_crm, legal_billing and legal_trust bring it to 15 tabs, 12 tables, 12 smart buttons

performance.how: Measured in Chromium on the built demos (MacBook, the machine shared with other lanes' runs): opening is the viewer's timeFirstPaint (main-thread work from mount to the paint that shows the page); a tab switch and a keystroke are e2e/real-legal.spec.ts's harness, the work from the event to the paint after it (e2e/perf.spec.ts's method). 14 tab switches and 11 keystrokes per run.

open.legalCaseMs: 196–215 when the machine is quiet (235–260 with the wait for the frame); 242–306 inside the e2e runs
open.forComparison: the Sales order example 93–99 ms, the Survey page 87–89 ms
open.why: Before: every tab was built at mount and only hidden — all 15 panels and 12 AG Grids, 4,393 DOM elements. Now a tab's parts are built when it is first shown, so opening builds the header and one tab: inside the e2e, the timing test's opening went from 370–475 ms to 93–120 ms, measured side by side with the old build on the same machine.

tabSwitch.medianMs: 21–26 in all four frameworks (before: 18–26 side by side); the harness shows each tab once, so every switch it times is a first show that builds the tab
tabSwitch.maxMs: 55–65 (a tab whose grids are built and drawn for the first time)

keystroke.medianMs: 5.2–8.9 in all four frameworks (before: 20.7–22.5 side by side)
keystroke.note: A tab out of sight is no longer brought up to date as values change, only when shown again; and a table hidden as display: none no longer measures itself every frame (AG Grid did, 120 frames a second each, idle or not). Under the one-frame (16 ms) budget.

performance.verdict: Quick: opening about a quarter of before, a keystroke well within one frame; the first show of each tab carries its own building.

wayfinding.flectra: Flectra's notebook wraps its 15 tab labels onto a second line, so every tab is in sight; the smart buttons open each related list in its own view.
fieldia: The 15 tab labels sit on one line that scrolls sideways: 1,466 px of labels in a 974 px strip at a 1,440 px window, so Billing, Trust, Timesheets, Correspondence and Internal are out of sight; but the tabs fade out at an edge with more past it, under a button that scrolls the strip along (right to left too, and at a phone's width, where 3 tabs show). Shown in the e2e.
A tab chosen however — a click, the arrow keys, Home or End, or a step's goTo — is scrolled into sight in the strip: after Close Case, the Outcome tab's label is in view.
The stat buttons double as a way in: Hearings, Tasks, Expenses, Documents, POAs, Hours, Correspondence and Trust Balance open their tab (goTo).
Help texts show under their fields (Flectra keeps them in a tooltip), so the header groups run to about 1,500 px and the tabs start below the fold of a 900 px window.
Arrow keys, Home and End move along the tab strip, and a hidden tab (Outcome, Contract Reviews) leaves no gap.
